title: No One's Crazy
supportedClaims: People bring different money histories to the table, so behavior that looks irrational from one life can look sensible from another.
The chapter argues that what someone lived through, inflation, boom years, layoffs, or easy markets, quietly defines what risk and reward feel like to them.
The practical move is to ask what game another person is playing and what memories taught them that game before judging their choices too quickly.
caution: Empathy is not relativism. Some choices are still poor, but they make more sense once their emotional origin is visible.
